No, it's not - and people are still using it, for their specific technical reasons (e.g. mounted filesystem performance limitations between Windows and WSL2). 

Anyway, this is how to install version that's ok with WSL1 (maybe some later one is ok, too; I haven't tried all the recents):

```
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash -s -- --version 1.14.20
```

💁 You probably also want to disable auto-update in your settings, probably at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "autoupdate": false,
  // ...
}
```

## Confirmed + additional data points (Rafael, April 28 2026)

Spent several hours debugging this today. Adding findings that might help the maintainers and other users hitting this.

### Models affected vs. working (tested via `opencode run --model X "hello"` from terminal)

| Model | Status |
|-------|--------|
| `opencode/kimi-k2.5` | ❌ Insufficient balance |
| `opencode/kimi-k2.6` | ❌ Insufficient balance |
| `opencode/glm-5.1` | ❌ Insufficient balance |
| `opencode/glm-5` | ❌ (presumed same upstream) |
| `opencode/minimax-m2.5` | ✅ Works |
| `opencode/minimax-m2.5-free` | ✅ Works |

So it's not just Kimi/Moonshot — **GLM/ZhipuAI upstream accounts are also depleted**. At least two separate upstream provider accounts are affected simultaneously.

### What the error looks like at the terminal level

```
opencode run --model opencode/kimi-k2.5 "hello"
Error: Insufficient balance. Manage your billing here: https://opencode.ai/workspace/wrk_.../billing
```

This is especially confusing because:
- Go plan dashboard shows **0% continuous / 0% weekly / 0% monthly** usage
- Invoice balance is $0.00 but that's expected for Go plan users
- `opencode auth list` shows active credential

### Root cause (confirmed from issue #24470)

The `org-446a70bb...` in the error is **OpenCode's own upstream Moonshot/ZhipuAI account**, not the user's account. The Go plan subscribers have no way to distinguish "my quota is exhausted" from "OpenCode's infrastructure account ran out."

### Workaround confirmed

Switch default model to `opencode/minimax-m2.5` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and in any agent configs (`~/.config/opencode/oh-my-openagent.json`). MiniMax upstream account appears funded.

### Request

It would help to have a status page or in-CLI notification distinguishing infrastructure failures from user billing issues. The current error message sends users chasing their own billing when the problem is on OpenCode's side.

Today's incident: a `task`-spawned `@general` subagent parsing an `.xls` rent-roll hung at exactly the pattern @timvw described —

* 22:07:11 task delegated to subagent
* 22:07:14 → 22:08:22 normal tool turns (read, bash, edit, retries)
* 22:08:27 message 10 emits a `step-start` with `parts=0`
* No `step-finish` ever arrived (verified for 30+ min via `GET /session/{id}/message`)

Sibling subagents in the same parent session continued running fine, so the hang is per sub-session — consistent with @yehudacohen's gap-1 analysis: the model-API call inside that single subagent's turn never returned, no timeout caught it.

We worked around the missing default by setting `provider.<name>.options.timeout = 300000` in our config for `anthropic` / `openai` / `google` — that turns this from a multi-hour hang into a 5-minute fail (which we can retry). Useful interim mitigation for anyone else hitting this.

I ran into the same issue and asked OpenCode to investigate:

> What's happening
> 1. OpenCode auto-selects github-copilot/gpt-5-mini as your small_model (per the priority list in the binary).
> 2. For title generation, OpenCode sends reasoning_effort: "minimal" (it wants the cheapest/fastest call).
> 3. GitHub Copilot's gpt-5-mini endpoint rejects "minimal" — it only accepts low, medium, or high. The request 400s.
> 4. The error is swallowed silently (no retry, no fallback), so the session keeps its placeholder title New session - <timestamp>.
> This is a Copilot-side API change — gpt-5-mini used to accept minimal. Your DB confirms it: every session through April 12 got a real title; everything April 15 and later is stuck as "New session - ...".
> 
> Fix
> Pin small_model to one that doesn't get a reasoning_effort: "minimal" rejection. Add to ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json:
> "small_model": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5"

I added `"small_model": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5",` to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and it fixed it.

63GiB with 100+ conversations is a clear memory management problem in long-running agent sessions. We operate 221 agents in daemon mode at [KinthAI](https://kinthai.ai) and had to solve OOM issues at scale.

**Root causes (likely):**

1. **Unbounded conversation history** — each conversation accumulates messages in memory. At 100+ conversations with potentially thousands of messages each, the in-memory representation grows without bound. The fix: context compaction. We use a three-tier progressive approach: recent turns stay full, older turns get summarized, very old turns get one-line digests. This caps memory per conversation at ~50KB regardless of length.

2. **Embedding cache growth** — if the agent caches embeddings for semantic retrieval, 100+ conversations worth of embeddings can easily reach 10-20GiB. The fix: LRU eviction on the embedding cache with a configurable max size.

3. **Tool result accumulation** — large tool outputs (file reads, API responses) stored in conversation history. A single 1MB file read stored 100 times across conversations = 100MB. The fix: tool results should be summarized at storage time, not stored raw.

**Practical solution for long-running sessions:**

- Set a per-conversation memory cap (e.g., 100 messages in full, older messages compacted)
- Set a global memory ceiling for the process and trigger garbage collection when approaching it
- Use persistent storage (SQLite) for conversation history instead of keeping everything in RAM — load on demand

We documented the memory architecture that prevents OOM: [Why Character.AI Forgets You — And What Persistent Memory Actually Requires](https://blog.kinthai.ai/why-character-ai-forgets-you-persistent-memory-architecture)
